Gowans Auctions, Moonah. Weekly Friday auction, Fri 16 Oct 2026, live from 10:00 AM (absentee bids close 9:30 AM)

Gowans Friday auction

All 1,608 lots were scanned with every photo viewed, blind rescored, and 132 candidates got a market pass with an Opus check. This time Gowans' own past results were the first source for every lot, so most maximum bids rest on what this room actually pays. It is a solid but modest sale: the best-supported picks are a Giant carbon full-suspension 29er (lot 1341), a run of gold rings and pieces with plenty of Gowans comps (lots 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10), a Victorian cedar secretaire bookcase (461), an original Xbox Crystal (769), six teak dining chairs (721), six 1966 round 50c coins (123) and a bag of watches with two Omega quartz pieces (171). The biggest unknown is lot 1408, a Giant Trance X Advanced Pro 29 carbon trail bike: no Gowans sale to compare, so no maximum bid, but worth a close look at inspection. Absentee bid counts were refreshed on Wednesday evening and will keep rising until Friday. Online absentee bids close at 9:30 AM Friday.

Assumptions
  • All 1,608 lots in the auction were taken from Gowans' public API and image store and scanned with every photo viewed. None was unscanned.
  • This is a live room auction. The site shows no prices, only a count of absentee bids on each lot (refreshed Wed 14 Oct, evening), so no current bid is used. Scoring is blind to price. The bid count shows interest, not how high bids go.
  • Buyer's premium is 19.8% including GST on the hammer price for all lots except vehicles, per the auction's own notice. All-in = hammer x 1.198.
  • Candidates with a blind score of 4 or more (132 lots) got a market pass. Other candidates and the lots the scan skipped appear in the table of every lot with a photo finding and a reason.
  • Gowans past results come from Gowans' public lot API, where sale_price is in cents and read as the hammer price (premium extra); dates are listing dates, about a week before each sale.
  • Other sold prices come from auction and marketplace data (PriceCharting for games and toys, popsike for hi-fi and others) that may not say whether premium is included. Maximum bids use only sold prices in the last 24 months.
  • Gold and silver weights, carat marks and maker claims in the titles are catalogue claims. Check weights and hallmarks at the inspection. Melt value is a floor, not a sale, so it never sets a maximum bid.
  • Pickup from 37 Main Road, Moonah. Inbound freight is assumed to be $0 because you are local.
  • Sources closed to this session (eBay, Wine-Searcher, Australian Whisky Auctions) were not used directly.

Working and confidence

Why Medium: Bumper Bash and Maxi-15 labels read, and several dated SOLD records seen on opened PriceCharting pages. But these are mostly US eBay sales through an aggregator, nothing is tested, the Bumper Bash label is worn and the black item is unconfirmed.

Dropped entries: Dropped: Gowans 413752 ($100), whose photo shows PS3, Xbox 360 and Wii discs, so it is not comparable. Dropped the PlayStation multi-lot entry: its price was given two ways ($80 and 7000 cents) and our lot has only one PS1 game. Dropped the GT64 entry: snippet only, and the PAL page gave no price. Dropped the UNSOLD placeholder. Moved the PriceCharting guide figures to ASKING and added dated SOLD records for Bumper Bash, Maxi-15 and the Expansion Pak. The researcher wrongly called the Maxi-15 an Atari multicart; it is an NES cart.

Working: Keep: lowest 24-month sales of the two label-confirmed items, Bumper Bash US$58.46 + Maxi-15 US$27.56 = US$86.02 x 1.433 = A$123.27; /1.198 = 102.9, round down to $100. Flip: resale about A$107 (Bumper Bash, worn label) + A$72 (Maxi-15) = A$179, less 13.4% eBay fees (A$24) and 2 parcels at A$12 = A$131; /2.396 = 54.7, round down to $55. A confirmed, working Expansion Pak would lift the flip maximum to about $80.

Ask Gowans: Is the black item with the red end an official Nintendo 64 Expansion Pak (label NUS-007)? Is the Bumper Bash label intact apart from fading? Is the Theme Park disc present and clean? Has anything been tested?

If Gowans confirms a weight W grams of marked 9ct (excluding the pendant stone), a sensible ceiling is about W x $50 hammer (all-in W x $60, near refiner value). At a guessed 5-7g that is $250-350 hammer, but this is a guess until weighed.

Ask Gowans: Could you give the total weight of the gold items (excluding the pendant stone), confirm which pieces are marked 9ct or 375 (especially the Mizpah half and the large hoop earring), and show or describe the brooch mentioned in the title? Is the pendant stone opal or an imitation?
